cues: Silver chloride, horn silver, is made by adding a chloride to silver nitrate.
It is white, curdy, and insoluble in water and dilute nitric acid.
But it dissolves in three reagents, all by forming complexes: ammonia, sodium thiosulphate, which is how photographs are fixed, and potassium cyanide.
